reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker actively promotes OneCoin as a cryptocurrency opportunity using extraordinary company-size and personal-earnings claims, including that it generated billions in revenue and doubled his employment income in less than two months. He directs viewers to join through the supplied signup link and explicitly urges them to take action and participate, rather than presenting the claims as criticism or investigation.

citations.quote: Welcome to OneCoin. The fastest company every tier at over a billion dollars in revenue, And the second-largest cryptocurrency in the world
For less than two months I made doubled than my job so I think that's a big opportunity for my friends and family all over the World.
Take action and be a part of the evolution.
Join: https://www.onecoin.eu/signup/crowndiamondteam.

opening.argument: The presentation uses opportunity and evolution language, not an explicit promise that viewers will receive a fixed return. The speaker places OneCoin within a broader account of cryptocurrency, describing how Bitcoin developed and how banks are examining blockchain technology. Even the personal result is presented as his experience and opinion about an opportunity, rather than a guarantee for every viewer. The material therefore can be read as enthusiastic commentary on an emerging financial technology, where viewers must assess the claims for themselves, not as a statement that success is certain.

citations.quote: This is the story of cryptocurrency and how it's evolved.
For less than two months I made doubled than my job so I think that's a big opportunity for my friends and family all over the World.
Citigroup have come out and they're creating their very own coin.
This is a win win situation for everyone, whoever is part of this opportunity.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The signup link and the closing invitation show that the video is promotional, but promotion alone does not establish deception or a guaranteed return. The cited earnings statement is explicitly framed as the speaker's own experience and opinion, while the company-size statements are claims about market status rather than promises that every viewer will profit. The prosecution also does not identify any stated guarantee, required payment, or promised outcome.

citations.quote: so I think that's a big opportunity for my friends and family all over the World.
whoever is part of this opportunity.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of the word 'guarantee' does not neutralize the overall financial message. The speaker combines a claimed rapid doubling of his job income with claims of billions in revenue and tells viewers to take action. That framing presents participation as an attractive route to financial gain, while the signup link supplies a direct path to join; cautionary wording is not actually provided.

citations.quote: For less than two months I made doubled than my job
The fastest company every tier at over a billion dollars in revenue
Take action and be a part of the evolution.
Join: https://www.onecoin.eu/signup/crowndiamondteam.

opening.argument: The video's stated structure is educational: the speaker says he is explaining the story and evolution of cryptocurrency, then compares Bitcoin's early transactions, later valuation, blockchain activity, and the emergence of cryptocurrency 2.0. References to banks and technology support a technology-and-market explainer reading. OneCoin appears as the example used to illustrate that evolution, while the speaker's first-person account supplies context about why he considers it significant. On the supplied evidence, this can be treated as educational commentary about digital currency rather than proof of a deceptive scheme.

citations.quote: This is the story of cryptocurrency and how it's evolved.
The very first transactions were made for 2 pizza.
A consortium called RF3 that is a consortium of the biggest banks in the world that are looking into the blockchain technology that is cryptocurrency.
Cryptocurrency 2.0 is born.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the subject a story or evolution does not make the presentation a neutral tutorial. The speaker shifts from historical background to welcoming viewers to OneCoin, reports his own income increase, gives company and ranking claims, provides a signup destination, and closes with a call to act. Those are substantive participation cues, not merely a demonstration of how cryptocurrency technology works.

citations.quote: Welcome to OneCoin.
For less than two months I made doubled than my job
Take action and be a part of the evolution.
Join: https://www.onecoin.eu/signup/crowndiamondteam.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The historical introduction is context for the pitch, not the video's operative purpose. The speaker does not teach a technical process or objectively test OneCoin; he links the example to rapid personal earnings, company revenue, and an instruction to participate. The educational framing therefore does not change that viewers are directed toward a financial opportunity through the supplied join link.

citations.quote: This company has $2 billion in revenue and is the world's second largest cryptocurrency in the world.
For less than two months I made doubled than my job
Take action and be a part of the evolution.
Join: https://www.onecoin.eu/signup/crowndiamondteam.

opening.argument: At most, the supplied material shows ordinary promotion of a cryptocurrency-related company and a referral destination. It does not show a deposit request, a guaranteed return, instructions to recruit a downline, a credential request, or a concrete transaction that transfers money. The description says only to join, and the speech discusses company revenue, technology, banks, and the speaker's own experience. Those omissions matter: a bold commercial claim or referral is not by itself evidence that the underlying service is a scam.

citations.quote: Join: https://www.onecoin.eu/signup/crowndiamondteam.
This company has $2 billion in revenue and is the world's second largest cryptocurrency in the world.
A consortium called RF3 that is a consortium of the biggest banks in the world that are looking into the blockchain technology that is cryptocurrency.
This is a win win situation for everyone, whoever is part of this opportunity.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The absence of a spoken deposit instruction does not make the promotion ordinary. The video gives viewers a direct join link and pairs participation with extraordinary growth and earnings claims. The claimed category does not require the speaker to display every operational step of a scam in the same clip; the relevant point is that token participation is marketed as an opportunity associated with rapid financial gain.

citations.quote: Join: https://www.onecoin.eu/signup/crowndiamondteam.
For less than two months I made doubled than my job
The fastest company every tier at over a billion dollars in revenue

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing mechanism is not the only issue. The material expressly identifies OneCoin, claims billions in revenue and a leading cryptocurrency position, reports that the speaker more than doubled his job income, and directs viewers to join. Calling this ordinary commerce cannot explain why unsupported financial success claims and a participation pathway are central to the message.
